skill.name: debug-cuda-crash
skill.description: Tutorial for diagnosing FlashInfer CUDA crashes with API logging and CUDA debugging tools.
skill.summary: Diagnose FlashInfer CUDA crashes by logging API inputs, tensor metadata, and numerical statistics.
skill.author: flashinfer-ai

security_audit.summary: The static external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced tutorial examples, not executable Ruby or shell code. I found no prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent. The main residual issue is that local debug logs may contain sensitive tensor metadata, statistics, or system details.

remediation.issue: Debug logs can include tensor metadata, value statistics, and system information.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear warning to store logs locally, review contents before sharing, and delete logs after debugging.

remediation.issue: Diagnostic command examples could be mistaken for automatic execution guidance.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands are examples for trusted user environments and should run only with user approval.

semantic_findings.title: Local Debug Logs May Expose Tensor Data
semantic_findings.description: The tutorial tells users to capture input tensors and write tensor metadata or statistics to logs. These local logs can expose sensitive model inputs, shapes, values, or system details if shared without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation explicitly recommends capturing tensors and persisting crash logs. The behavior is local and diagnostic, so the risk is limited to accidental disclosure.

content.value_statement: CUDA crashes often hide the input data that caused the failure. This skill shows how to use FlashInfer API logging and CUDA tools to isolate the failing call.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to enable FlashInfer API logging with FLASHINFER_LOGLEVEL and FLASHINFER_LOGDEST.
Shows how to inspect tensor shapes, dtypes, devices, and statistics before crashes.
Covers illegal memory access, NaN or Inf values, out of memory errors, and dtype mismatches.
Demonstrates multi-process log file patterns for torchrun workflows.
Shows how to combine logging with compute-sanitizer, cuda-gdb, and kernel printf debugging.
limitations: Does not execute diagnostics or inspect a live GPU environment by itself.
Applies to FlashInfer APIs that use the @flashinfer_api logging decorator.
Log contents can expose sensitive tensor metadata and statistics if shared.
Examples assume familiarity with PyTorch, CUDA, and shell environment variables.

use_cases.title: Trace a CUDA crash
use_cases.description: Use API logging to find the last FlashInfer call and inspect its input tensors.

use_cases.title: Investigate numerical instability
use_cases.description: Use tensor statistics to locate NaN, Inf, or extreme values before a failing operation.

use_cases.title: Debug distributed GPU jobs
use_cases.description: Create separate process logs and compare ranks when a multi-GPU run fails.

prompt_templates.title: Enable basic crash logging
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single script crash.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through enabling FlashInfer API logging for a CUDA crash in my PyTorch script. I want to capture the last API call and input metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret a crash log
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a saved FlashInfer debug log.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a FlashInfer API log from a failed run. Help me inspect tensor shapes, dtypes, devices, and the first failed call.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose numerical failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Find NaN or Inf values before a CUDA failure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me use level 5 FlashInfer logging to investigate NaN or Inf values in this CUDA workflow. Explain what patterns to compare.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an advanced CUDA debug session
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine API logs with CUDA debugging tools.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step plan that combines FlashInfer API logging, compute-sanitizer, cuda-gdb, and selective kernel printf output.

output_examples.input: A FlashInfer decode job fails with an illegal memory access after several successful calls.
output_examples.output: The assistant identifies the last API call without output, compares query and cache shapes, and recommends fixing a head dimension mismatch.

output_examples.input: A multi-GPU training run crashes only on one rank.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends per-process log files, compares rank logs, and isolates the rank with an unexpected tensor size.

output_examples.input: A model returns NaN after a FlashInfer operation.
output_examples.output: The assistant recommends statistics logging, checks value ranges, and narrows the issue to the first tensor with NaN or Inf counts.

best_practices: Start with level 3 logging before enabling heavier statistics.
Write crash logs to local files and remove them after analysis.
Disable logging before production runs to reduce noise and exposure.
anti_patterns: Sharing debug logs without checking for sensitive tensor metadata.
Running heavy memory checkers before narrowing the failing API call.
Assuming every FlashInfer API has logging before confirming decorator support.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a tutorial that explains diagnostic commands for users to run in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it fix CUDA bugs directly?
faq.answer: No. It helps identify likely causes so a developer can update code, tensor shapes, or runtime settings.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers FlashInfer API logging, compute-sanitizer, cuda-gdb, torchrun log separation, and CUDA kernel printf debugging.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this workflow?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill gives structured guidance that these assistants can apply when reviewing CUDA crash reports.

faq.question: Are debug logs safe to share?
faq.answer: Review logs first. They may include tensor metadata, value statistics, system information, and file paths.

faq.question: When should logging be disabled?
faq.answer: Disable logging after debugging, especially before production or benchmark runs where logs add noise and exposure.
